title: README test count overstated 6× ('10800+' vs actual ~1948)
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area4).

README.md line 496 (Test section) claims `# 10800+ tests (108 Bennett integration, 74 pixel renderer, 53 ASCII drawer)`. Static `@test\b` count audit:
- 1,753 tests across the 62 files included in runtests.jl
- 1,948 tests across all 71 test files (including the 9 orphans tracked under bead 4gom)

1. Decide the canonical count metric — static `@test` count, or runtime test count from `Test.PASS_COUNT[]`.

title: test_bennett_integration.jl — 3 known-failing tests not @test_broken (silent red)
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area4).

`test/test_bennett_integration.jl` has three tests at lines 291, 302, 344 that are KNOWN to be failing today (confirmed by orchestrator during session 74 regression check):

```
x+1 Int8 (26 wires): @test _CIRCUIT_INC.n_wires <= 30  → Evaluated: 41 <= 30
x+3 Int8 (26 wires): @test _CIRCUIT_ADD3.n_wires <= 30 → Evaluated: 41 <= 30
estimate_oracle_resources:   @test r.qubits == 26     → Evaluated: 41 == 26
```

These are not marked `@test_broken` — so the suite exits with 'Some tests did not pass' and CI reports a red run for what is actually a known upstream Bennett.jl wire-count drift (Bennett v0.5+ produces 41 wires for these cases vs the test's expected 26).

## Fix

Decide:

A. **The expectation is wrong** — Bennett's wire count for these cases is now 41 (its general LLVM lowering uses more ancillae than expected). Update the assertion to match reality and add an inline comment explaining the upstream change.

B. **The expectation is right and Bennett regressed.** File a Bennett-side bead, mark these tests `@test_broken` with reference to the upstream issue, and CI is green again.

C. **The Sturm.jl-pw9/ao1 fix lands and the wire count drops back.** Same as B but with explicit pointer to the followup bead.

Whatever the choice, the suite should not silent-red.

- bead ao1 (hand-rolled QROM) — would directly drop wire counts for QROM path but does not affect oracle(x+1) or oracle(x+3) paths

title: Document docs/literature vs docs/physics policy + ship missing N&C 5.2 / Vedral distillations
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (areas 3 + 4).

CLAUDE.md Rule 4: 'Physics = LOCAL PDF + EQUATION. Grounded in physics means: a local PDF copy of the paper lives in docs/physics/, and the implementation references an explicit equation from that paper.'

Two issues:

### 1. docs/literature/ is the de-facto second tier, but undocumented

`.gitignore` excludes `docs/literature/**/*.pdf`. ~15 src files in `simulation/`, `block_encoding/`, `qsvt/` cite `docs/literature/...` paths. Those PDFs are not in the repo, by policy. The two-tier system (committed distillations in `docs/physics/`, gitignored bulk PDFs in `docs/literature/`) is not described anywhere — neither in CLAUDE.md Rule 4 nor in README. New contributors hit a Rule 4 violation that is actually compliant by an unwritten policy.

### 2. Two committed distillations are missing

- `docs/physics/nielsen_chuang_5.2.md` — referenced by `src/library/patterns.jl:134` (phase_estimate docstring). §5.1 and §5.3 distillations are present; §5.2 is the critical gap for Shor.
- `docs/physics/vedral_1996_adder.md` — referenced by `src/types/qint.jl:196`.

## Fix

1. **Update CLAUDE.md Rule 4** to describe the two-tier policy explicitly:
   - `docs/physics/` — committed: short Markdown distillations of paper theorems/equations (referenced by source docstrings); the canonical project-side reference.
   - `docs/literature/` — gitignored: full paper PDFs for offline reading; useful for first-time setup but not required to be in-repo.
   - Source docstrings MAY reference both: a `docs/physics/foo.md` distillation as the project-side citation, and a `docs/literature/foo.pdf` deeplink for the original.
   - The committed `docs/physics/foo.md` MUST exist for any cited paper.

2. **Write the two missing distillations** for N&C §5.2 (phase estimation) and Vedral 1996 (quantum adder).

3. **Audit existing src docstrings** that reference `docs/literature/...` only — verify the corresponding `docs/physics/...md` distillation also exists; create stubs where it doesn't.

## Test

Add a runtests.jl boot lint that greps src for `docs/physics/.*\.md` and asserts each path resolves to a real file in `docs/physics/`.

title: Rule 11 violations: raw apply_*! calls on bare WireID in 4 library sites
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area3).

PRD Rule 11 mandates 4-primitives-only on QBool/QInt operators. The following library sites bypass the DSL by reaching into raw WireID + ctx.apply_*!:

| File | Function | ~Line | Call |
|------|----------|-------|------|
| src/library/coset.jl | _coset_init! | ~74 | apply_ry!(ctx, pad_anc[p+1], π/2) |
| src/library/coset.jl | _runway_init! | ~125 | apply_ry!(ctx, reg.wires[W+p+1], π/2) |
| src/library/patterns.jl | find Bennett path | ~515 | apply_rz!(ctx, output_wires[1], π) |
| src/library/shor.jl | _shor_mulmod_a! | ~363-370 | apply_cx!(ctx, z_wires[i], y_wires[i]) ×2 |

Per CLAUDE.md Rule 11: 'A subagent that constructs a gate from a raw matrix is WRONG.' Same logic applies to bare WireID + apply_*! — the DSL surface is QBool.θ/.φ/⊻=. Bypassing it loses the type safety, the global-phase audit (cf. NOTGate twv/Y bug), and the literate documentation.

## Fix pattern

Wrap WireID in QBool, then use operator syntax:
```julia
# Before:
apply_ry!(ctx, pad_anc[p+1], π/2)
# After:
q = QBool(pad_anc[p+1], ctx, false)
q.θ += π/2
```

For shor.jl _shor_mulmod_a! 3-CNOT swaps: use `swap!(QBool(...), QBool(...))` from gates.jl.

## Test

Add a 'No raw WireID in library code' lint test that greps src/library/*.jl for `apply_(ry|rz|cx)!` and fails. Could be a runtest assertion at boot.

## Refs

- bead hfm (existing P3, P5 hygiene sweep) — should escalate to P0 and bundle with this fix
- area3 review report Cross-Cutting Finding 2
close_reason: Fixed in commit 31d9755. All 8 sites converted to QBool primitive syntax; new test_rule11_lint.jl pins the contract at CI time.

title: control/cases.jl _cases_dispatch lacks try/finally — exception corrupts TracingContext
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area1).

`src/control/cases.jl` _cases_dispatch(::TracingContext) swaps `ctx.dag` in/out without try/finally. Any exception inside `then()` or `else_()` leaves `ctx.dag` pointing at a partial branch vector, permanently corrupting the TracingContext.

## Fix

```julia
saved = ctx.dag
ctx.dag = then_branch_dag
try
    then()
finally
    ctx.dag = saved
end
```

Same for else_ branch.

## Test

Add to test_cases.jl a test that triggers an exception inside the then-branch and asserts the context is still usable.

## Refs
- area1 finding P1-A1.2
close_reason: Fixed in commit 613050a. try/finally around both branch dispatches; ctx.dag restored on exception; new regression tests pin the contract.

title: DensityMatrixContext measure! upper-triangle write + per-element FFI hot loop
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area1).

`src/context/density.jl` DensityMatrixContext.measure! has TWO bugs that combine:

1. **Upper-triangle write corruption.** The reset-to-|0⟩ post-collapse iterates all (r,c) including the upper triangle via `ctx.orkan[r,c] = val`. In MIXED_PACKED format the upper-triangle setter may silently no-op or write to wrong memory, leaving the post-measurement state corrupted. Needs verification against orkan's MIXED_PACKED layout.

2. **Per-element FFI in O(4^n) loop.** Same root cause as bead 059 (already fixed for EagerContext). Probability + collapse use per-element `ctx.orkan[r,c]` FFI accessors in nested loops over all (r,c) pairs — n_qubits=6 means 4096 ccalls per measure!. Catastrophic at n>=6.

## Fix

Apply the bead-059 pattern: `unsafe_wrap` over the MIXED_PACKED amplitude buffer, do the loops in pure Julia, write back atomically. For the upper-triangle issue: write only the lower triangle (or full triangle if MIXED_PACKED stores both), and verify the layout against orkan's docs.

## Test

Add a regression test that measures a MIXED state and checks the post-measurement density matrix exactly equals the projection. Statistical test N>=1000 per outcome.

## Refs

- bead 059 (closed) — same fix for EagerContext
- area1 review report finding P0-A1.3 + P1-A1.1
close_reason: Fixed in commit 681c1d7. unsafe_wrap pattern from bead 059 applied; lower-triangle-only access; in-place |1⟩→|0⟩ reset. 4-qubit GHZ regression test added.

title: classical_type(::Type{<:QInt}) hardcoded to Int8 — silent truncation at W>8

title: orkan_channel_1q! missing _check_qubit before ccall (SIGABRT on bad index)
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area2).

`src/orkan/ffi.jl:247` orkan_channel_1q! is the only gate wrapper that omits the `_check_qubit` guard before its ccall. Every other wrapper has it (lines 154, 173, 186, 200, 201, 213, 214, 226, 227, 228 all show _check_qubit calls).

Per the comment in ffi.jl, Orkan calls `exit()` on bad qubit index — i.e., SIGABRTs the entire Julia process. With the missing guard, an OOB index in any noise channel call kills Julia with no Julia-side exception, no recoverable signal.

## Fix

Add `_check_qubit(state, target, :channel_1q)` at the top of orkan_channel_1q!:

```julia
function orkan_channel_1q!(state::OrkanStateRaw, sop::OrkanSuperopRaw, target::Integer)
    _check_qubit(state, target, :channel_1q)
    @ccall LIBORKAN.channel_1q(...)
    nothing
end
```

## Test

Add to test_orkan.jl: `@test_throws ErrorException orkan_channel_1q!(state, sop, 100)` (where state has only ~10 qubits).

## Refs

- area2 review report finding P0-A2.4
close_reason: Fixed in commit 09bbcf2. Standard _check_qubit guard added; @test_throws probe pins the contract.

title: noise/channels.jl _apply_kraus! missing GC.@preserve around pointer(data)
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area2).

`src/noise/channels.jl` _apply_kraus! captures a raw Julia pointer into `OrkanKrausRaw` and calls into C with no `GC.@preserve` wrapping the ccall. The Julia GC may collect the underlying `data` array between pointer capture and the ccall, producing a dangling read that silently corrupts the density matrix.

Verified: zero `GC.@preserve` calls in the entire Sturm.jl codebase. This is concerning more broadly — every other ccall site that passes a Julia-owned pointer should also be audited.

## Fix

Wrap the FFI call in `GC.@preserve data ...`:

```julia
GC.@preserve data begin
    sop = orkan_kraus_to_superop(kraus)
    try
        orkan_channel_1q!(ctx.orkan.raw, sop, qubit)
    finally
        orkan_superop_free!(sop)
    end
end
```

## Audit

Grep all of src/ for raw `pointer(...)` or `unsafe_convert(Ptr{...}, ...)` followed by `@ccall` and verify each is GC-safe. `unsafe_wrap` cases should also have GC anchors when the source is a Julia array.

## Reproduction

Hard to reproduce reliably — requires GC pressure during the narrow window. Stress test: run a depolarising-noise loop with N>1000 iterations and concurrent allocations on another task.

## Refs

- area2 review report at .claude/reviews/2026-04-27/area2_ir_compilation.md, finding P0-A2.2
close_reason: Fixed in commit 1d143a7. GC.@preserve added around pointer(data) lifetime in _apply_kraus!. Audit of unsafe_wrap sites in eager/density showed they wrap Orkan-owned (not Julia-owned) memory and are safe under current usage. Stress-test deferred — race not deterministically reproducible.

title: Bennett NOTGate emits Ry(π)=-iY instead of X — controlled-oracle phase corruption
description:
P0 from 2026-04-27 review (area2). 

`src/bennett/bridge.jl:81` lowers Bennett's NOTGate to `apply_ry!(ctx, wm[g.target], π)`. The line comment claims this is the X gate. It isn't: `Ry(π) = -iY`, not X. Det differs by a sign.

Inside `when(ctrl)`, this becomes controlled-Ry(π), NOT controlled-X. The relative phase between the ctrl=|0⟩ and ctrl=|1⟩ branches is wrong. This is exactly the Session 8 bug documented in CLAUDE.md 'Global Phase and Universality'. Every `oracle(f, q)` call inside `when(ctrl)` with ctrl in superposition produces a wrong relative phase. Invisible in any computational-basis test; corrupts every controlled oracle path. The same bug exists at `src/passes/deferred_measurement.jl:51,55` (false-branch X via RyNode(wire,π)) — fix should land at both sites simultaneously.

Sturm's `X!` in `src/gates.jl:12` is correctly `q.φ += π; q.θ += π` = Rz(π)·Ry(π) (det=-1, correct X up to global phase that cancels under control). Bennett's NOTGate path skips the Rz(π).

## Reproduction

```julia
@context EagerContext() begin
    c = QBool(1/2)         # control in superposition
    a = QInt{2}(0)
    when(c) do
        # Any oracle that emits a Bennett NOTGate (e.g., loading a constant)
        # produces wrong phase between branches
        x = oracle(y -> y + 1, a)  
    end
end
```

## Fix

In `bridge.jl` _apply_bennett_gate! for NOTGate, replace with:
```julia
apply_rz!(ctx, wm[g.target], π)
apply_ry!(ctx, wm[g.target], π)
```

Same fix at deferred_measurement.jl lines 51, 55 (replace RyNode(wire, π) with RzNode(wire, π) + RyNode(wire, π)). Or land bead 7pz (atomic XNode) and emit XNode at both sites.

## Test

Add to `test_bennett_integration.jl` a controlled-oracle test that distinguishes Y and X under superposition control: prep |+⟩ control, run oracle, measure ctrl in X-basis. With X: deterministic. With Y: random.

## Refs

- CLAUDE.md 'Global Phase and Universality' section
- Session 8 bug history (Python sturm)
- Session 13 bug history (Sturm.jl Grover)
- bead 7pz (atomic XNode would also fix)
close_reason: Fix landed in commit 4b20721. Bennett NOTGate now emits Rz(π)·Ry(π) (matching not!), same at defer_measurements emit sites. Single-shot deterministic test added. Project-wide CI lint for standalone apply_ry!(...,π) recommended as follow-up.

title: Fix _coset_init!: state preparation produces wrong residue distribution
description: Q84 implementer used QFT-sandwich approach for _coset_init!. State-correctness probe (2026-04-20 session 35) shows only 13% of measurements give correct residue mod N (vs ~100% expected). Approach is conceptually wrong: pad qubits inside the QFT'd register cause control/target overlap. Implementer's 'self-wire Rz as unconditional' fix introduces spurious phases (controlled-Rz(θ) with ctrl=target=q ≡ diag(1, e^{iθ/2}) ≠ Rz(θ)).
design: Per Gidney 1905.08488 Fig 1, the InitCoset circuit uses SEPARATE pad qubits (not inside reg). Each pad starts |0⟩→H→|+⟩, controls +2^p·N into the value register, then comparison-negation (-1)^{x≥2^p·N} disentangles pad from value. Without comparison-negation the result is entangled state Σ_j |j⟩_pad ⊗ |k+jN⟩_reg — tracing out pad gives the correct mixed coset state where all measurements yield (k+jN) mod N = k. For 6xi residue tests this entangled state suffices. Comparison-negation can be added later for full pure-coset properties (deviation bound, +N near-eigenvector). REFACTOR: QCoset gets a pad_anc::NTuple{Cpad, WireID} field. Total internal qubits = W + 2·Cpad. The 'reg' field stays QInt{W+Cpad} for the value register. Discard! frees both reg.wires and pad_anc.
notes: Blocks Sturm.jl-6xi (coset bead). Q84 type design was correct in spirit but the impl had a subtle physics bug only catchable by state-correctness tests, not smoke tests.
close_reason: Fixed via external pad ancillae refactor. State-correctness verified: 100% correct residue (4000 shots, N=15, k=7, Cpad=3); all 8 basis states equiprobable within 3σ. Smoke tests still 60/60. Committed 234b8ef.

title: mulmod_beauregard! leaks phase on ctrl=|1⟩ branch (x-dependent)
description:
mulmod_beauregard! (Sturm.jl-uf4, Beauregard 2003 Fig. 7 c-U_a) leaks a phase on the ctrl=|1⟩ branch whenever x > 0, which decoheres ctrl when ancillas are discarded.  This breaks Shor's PE cascade at L ≥ 5 (N ≥ 21).

## Reproduction

```julia
# test/probe_mulmod_phase.jl (committed)
@context EagerContext() begin
    x = QInt{5}(x0)        # any x0 > 0
    ctrl = QBool(1/2)       # |+⟩
    mulmod_beauregard!(x, 2, 21, ctrl)
    ctrl.θ -= π/2          # Ry(-π/2) = inverse of QBool(1/2) prep
    m = Bool(ctrl)          # should be FALSE if ctrl preserved
end
```

Across 80-shot runs at all L=4,5 × various (a, N) × x0 in 1..N-1:
- x0 = 0  → 0% ctrl=true (clean)
- x0 > 0  → ~50% ctrl=true  ⇒  sin²(ξ/2) = 0.5  ⇒  ξ = π/2

## Why Session 25 uf4 tests missed it

Sturm.jl-uf4's acceptance tests (test/test_arithmetic.jl lines 229-295) measured ctrl in **Z basis** (Bool(ctrl) after mulmod with ctrl=|+⟩).  Z-basis measurement of |+⟩ and of a MAXIMALLY MIXED state both give 50/50 — the two are indistinguishable in Z.  A proper test needs **X-basis measurement** (Ry(-π/2) then Z, as in the probe above).

The Session 25 3208/3208 pass reflected arithmetic correctness and ctrl=|1⟩ / ctrl=|0⟩ identity, NOT coherence preservation of ctrl.

## Impact on Shor (Sturm.jl-6kx)

The PE cascade in shor_order_D calls mulmod_beauregard! t times, each with a different counter qubit as ctrl.  Each call leaks π/2 on the |1⟩ branch, entangling that counter qubit with the internal b/anc ancillae.  When those ancillae are discarded (at end of each mulmod), the counter qubit decoheres.

- **N=15 t=3** (Session 26 'passing' tests): only 2 of 3 mulmods fire (a_j = [7,4,1] skipped after saturation); accumulated decoherence happens to align with PE peaks, giving 50% r=4 hit rate — incidental.
- **N=21 t=6**: 6 mulmods fire (a_j = [2,4,16,4,16,4]); decoherence scrambles PE.  Measured 0/20 r=6 hits, 14/20 ‘other’ (vs expected 33% r=6).  See test/probe_shor_larger_N.jl (committed, failing) and test/probe_N21_ytilde.jl (ỹ histogram shows 30 distinct values across 40 shots, only 10 at theoretical peaks {0,11,21,32,43,53}).
- **N=35 t=6**: projected to fail for the same reason; not even reached due to N=21 failure upstream.

Session 26's Session-25-parallel claim 'all 3208 tests green' is correct but INSUFFICIENT as a correctness guarantee.

## Suspected sources of π/2 leak (not yet narrowed)

Candidates under investigation:
1. **controlled-Rz(θ) phase leak on superposed target.** For Rz(θ) applied to wire in superposition (Fourier basis), the ctrl=|1⟩ branch picks up -θ/2 global phase.  Inside modadd step 6 (`when(anc) add_qft!(y, N)`), anc picks up Σ_k -θ_k/2.  In modadd step 1/7/13 with ctrls=(ctrl, xj), ctrl picks up the leak per Rz fired.  The per-modadd leaks might sum to a constant π/2 depending on N, a, x.
2. **Ry(π) / Ry(-π) MSB flip at steps 9/11 of modadd.** Unconditional, but might interact with surrounding Fourier gates in a way that leaks under outer ctrls.
3. **add_qft! angle folding (mod(θ+π, 2π) - π).** Folding Rz(θ) → Rz(θ-2π) picks up global phase -1.  Under ctrl, -1 = e^{iπ} phase on |1⟩ branch.  Cumulative across L gates per add_qft! call, and 2L such calls per mulmod.

## Fix plan

1. Build a targeted X-basis test harness: pass ctrl=|+⟩ through each sub-block (add_qft!, modadd with ctrls, mulmod SWAP-under-when, full mulmod) and isolate where the π/2 enters.
2. Once located, apply the Beauregard convention-fix precedent from Session 25 (Ry(π)/Ry(-π) instead of X!) — likely another global-phase compensation.
3. Add X-basis regression tests to test/test_arithmetic.jl so future modifications can't silently break coherence.
4. Re-verify shor_order_D at N=15, N=21, N=35 end-to-end.

## Files

- `test/probe_mulmod_phase.jl` (new) — X-basis probe, reproduces the leak at L=4 N=15 and L=5 N=21.
- `test/probe_shor_larger_N.jl` (new) — N=21/N=35 end-to-end verification, currently FAILS.
- `test/probe_N21_ytilde.jl` (new) — ỹ histogram confirming PE is scrambled.
- `test/probe_shor_bug_hunt.jl` (new) — isolation: EXP-A (mulmod alone is correct at L=5), EXP-B (N=15 PE works at t=4), EXP-C (N=15 PE works at t=6).
- `test/probe_pe_bug.jl` (new) — confirms phase_estimate itself is correct; bug is mulmod-specific.

## Acceptance

- X-basis test on ctrl after mulmod_beauregard! returns <5% leak at all (L, N, a, x) within EagerContext budget.

title: OAA phase computation: direct Chebyshev-convention QSVT phases needed
description: The BS+NLFT pipeline doubles Chebyshev degree d→2d via analytic conversion. For T₃ (degree 3), this produces 7 analytic phases where only the first and last are non-zero — the 5 middle phases collapse to 0 due to the sparse analytic structure (c₀z⁰ + c₆z⁶). In the reflection QSVT circuit, the middle zero phases cause adjacent U/U† pairs to cancel, reducing the effective circuit to a single oracle call (P(x)=x). Root cause confirmed: post-selection rate is ~25% = (1/2)² for ALL test polynomials regardless of gap, matching P(x)=x exactly. Need direct Chebyshev-convention QSVT phases (3 phases for degree-3 T₃) that bypass the analytic conversion. This is the blocker for OAA amplitude amplification.
notes: ROOT CAUSE REFINED: Two issues found. (1) FIXED: BS+NLFT degree doubling collapses T₃ phases — solved with direct Chebyshev phases [-π, -π/2, π/2]. (2) NEW: qsvt_reflect! applies Rz on ancillas[1] only, which implements e^{iφZ₁}⊗I. For multi-ancilla BEs (like the lifted Thm56 circuit with 4 ancilla), OAA needs e^{iφ(2Π-I)} where Π=|0⟩⟨0|^⊗4 — a multi-qubit reflection, NOT a single-qubit Rz. This explains why OAA gives 5% on the real Hamiltonian (4 ancilla) but 100% on the synthetic (1 ancilla). Fix: implement a multi-ancilla OAA circuit that uses _multi_controlled_z! style reflections instead of single-qubit Rz.
close_reason: Fixed. Two bugs: (1) direct Chebyshev phases [-π,-π/2,π/2] bypass BS+NLFT degree doubling collapse, (2) _reflect_ancilla_phase! for multi-ancilla OAA reflections. Result: 72% success, 6.3x boost.

title: In-place compact_state! variant for Bennett ancilla bursts
description:
Follow-up to Sturm.jl-2qp investigation. The n_qubits ratchet during Bennett bursts cannot be reclaimed without an in-place compaction primitive that does NOT reallocate the Orkan statevector buffer.

## Problem

`apply_reversible!` allocates K Bennett ancillae (typically 3-7 for Sturm-side QROM lookups at c_mul ≤ 2), runs the compiled gates, then deallocates them via the per-deallocate threshold check (free_slots ≥ 8). For sub-threshold bursts the threshold is never crossed and n_qubits stays stuck at the burst peak. Subsequent gates between forward and uncompute QROM (`superpose!`, `add_qft_quantum!`, `interfere!` inside `_pep_mod_iter!`) run on a 4 GB statevector instead of the working-set 16 KB. Per-call wall time spikes from ~15 µs to ~86 ms.

Two naive fixes were tried in Session 74 and both regressed:
- compact at end of `apply_reversible!` → 75% slower (compact-then-regrow thrashing on the next QROM)
- compact at iteration boundary in `_pep_mod_iter!` → 0% c_mul=2, 2.3× regression on c_mul=1

## Required: logical-only compact

The compact has to drop n_qubits BETWEEN forward and uncompute QROM WITHOUT triggering _grow_state! on the next allocation. Concrete contract:

1. Reorganise wire_to_qubit so live wires map to indices [0, len-1]
2. Keep the Orkan buffer at its current capacity (no realloc, no GC)
3. Set n_qubits = len(live); subsequent gates only operate on the first 2^new_n amplitudes
4. Track logical free_slots so allocate! returns those indices first, only growing the Orkan buffer when logical slots run out

Cost per compaction: one in-place amplitude scatter (likely none, since freed Bennett ancillae are typically at high indices already). No malloc/free, no GC, no copy. Should be < 1 ms at n=28.

## Acceptance

- New API `compact_state_logical!(ctx::EagerContext)` (or kwarg on existing). Existing `compact_state!` semantics unchanged (it still does the buffer-shrinking variant).
- `apply_reversible!` calls the logical variant in its `finally` block.
- `probe_count_DE.jl` E c_mul=2 wall time drops from 192s to <30s (≥6× speedup).
- High-nq fraction (gates at n_qubits ≥ 24) drops from 26% to <5%.
- All existing tests pass (test_compact_state.jl, test_compact_state_dm.jl, test_bennett_integration.jl).

## Reference

WORKLOG Session 74 (2026-04-27) — full diagnostic data and rejected approaches.
Bead Sturm.jl-2qp — original investigation.
close_reason: Fixed in this commit. compact_state_logical! is in-place on the existing Orkan buffer; capacity unchanged; orkan.raw.qubits dropped to new_n via direct mutable-struct field write so gate ccalls operate on 2^new_n amplitudes. apply_reversible! calls it in finally after ancilla deallocates. allocate! bumps orkan.raw.qubits when ctx.n_qubits grows back. 24/24 in test_compact_state_logical.jl including a Bennett-path acceptance test (oracle_table call leaves n_qubits ≤ 4, capacity unchanged). No regressions in compact_state(_dm)/p9_auto_dispatch/arithmetic/qint/channel.

title: Profile shor_order_E per-gate slowdown vs shor_order_D_semi (~750× at N=15)
description:
## Observation

Per-DAG-gate wall time on `shor_order_E` (windowed arithmetic, GE21 §2.5) is
roughly 750× higher than `shor_order_D_semi` (Beauregard) at N=15, even
though E's abstract DAG has FEWER nodes per mulmod than D.

Recorded today (16 OMP threads, EagerContext + Orkan):

|                       | DAG nodes per mulmod | wall time per mulmod | per-gate wall time |
|-----------------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------------------|
| D (Beauregard) at N=15| 532 (12 CCX + 400 cRz + 120 ccRz) | ~250 ms      | ~0.5 ms            |
| E (windowed) at N=15  | 390 (130 CCX + 170 cRz + 90 ccRz) | 186 s (c_mul=2) / 74 s (c_mul=1) | ~480 ms     |

D sits where memory bandwidth predicts (16 MB statevector / 50 GB/s ≈ 0.3 ms).
E is three orders of magnitude off.

## Why this isn't statevector size

Peak live qubits: D-semi 12 (64 KB), E 20 (16 MB). 256× larger statevector
should cost ~4–8× per gate from cache effects, nowhere near 750×. Confirmed
the dominant factor lives below the DAG level, not in the obvious places
(memory bandwidth, gate count, peak qubit count).

## Hypotheses (in priority order, none confirmed)

1. **`qrom_lookup_xor!` fan-out** — one DAG "lookup" on a 2^c_mul-entry
   table likely expands to many primitive Orkan calls (multi-controlled
   XOR cascades over window address bits). Probe by timing a single
   `qrom_lookup_xor!` call in isolation vs counting its ccall events.
2. **`plus_equal_product_mod!` internal cascade** — windowed-add into
   coset register may have per-window inner controlled-adder cascade
   not surfaced in DAG node count.
3. **Per-ccall FFI / control-stack overhead** — if E's abstract gates fan
   out to many `apply_cx!`/`apply_ry!` calls with non-empty control
   stacks, the per-call Julia → cascade → ccall overhead multiplies.

## Investigation steps (no fix proposed yet)

1. Wrap `apply_cx!`/`apply_ry!`/`apply_rz!` with a counter + timer. Run one
   `_shor_mulmod_E_controlled!` and one `mulmod_beauregard!` at N=15. Compare
   primitive ccall counts to DAG node counts.
2. Run `_shor_mulmod_E_controlled!` under `perf record` (or Julia's
   `@profile`). Find the hot stack frame.
3. Time `qrom_lookup_xor!` and `plus_equal_product_mod!` in isolation via
   probes; quantify each layer's contribution.

## Why it matters

Blocks Sturm.jl-6oc's N=15 statistical acceptance criteria (criterion (a)
50-shot would take ~6 hours at observed timings). Blocks any future
windowed-arithmetic use at user-facing N. The MBU sweep
(probe_toffoli_cmul_sweep_mbu.jl) shows E's T-proxy beats D-semi from L=10
onwards — but those wins are inaccessible if simulation is too slow to
verify them statistically.

## Reproduction

  OMP_NUM_THREADS=16 LIBORKAN_PATH=... \
    julia --project /home/tobiasosborne/Projects/Sturm.jl/probe_mulmod_E_bench.jl

## Related

- Sturm.jl-6oc — windowed arithmetic Shor (closing alongside this bead's creation)
- Sturm.jl-059 — n_qubits ratchet fix (closed; gave 6.3× at N=15 c_mul=2 from
  ~21 min/mulmod down to ~3 min/mulmod, but the residual gap is what this
  bead investigates)
close_reason: Investigation complete. Hypotheses (i)/(ii)/(iii) all refuted; root cause is the n_qubits ratchet during sub-threshold Bennett bursts (gates between QROM forward + uncompute run on a 4 GB statevector at peak n_qubits=28, vs working-set 16 KB). Diagnostic counters added in src/context/eager.jl (reset_gate_counts! / gate_counts) plus 21 tests in test/test_bennett_compact.jl. Two naive fixes attempted and reverted (in apply_reversible! → 75% regression, at iteration boundary → 2.3× regression on c_mul=1) due to compact-then-regrow thrashing on the Orkan buffer. Architectural fix filed as Sturm.jl-pw9 (in-place / logical-only compact_state! variant). See WORKLOG Session 74 (2026-04-27) for full diagnostic data, probe_count_DE.jl for the harness.

title: [bug] X! and Y! are swapped in gates.jl — physics correctness violation (P3 ground rule)
description:
src/gates.jl defines X!(q) = Ry(π) which as a CHANNEL is Y (not X), and Y!(q) = Rz(π)·Ry(π) which is X (not Y). Verified via density-matrix action: X!(|+⟩) → |-⟩ (Y-channel behaviour; pure-X channel leaves |+⟩ invariant); Y!(|+⟩) → |+⟩ (X-channel behaviour).

Bug has been silent because: (1) on freshly-prepared |0⟩ qubits, Ry(π) and X give identical channels (both |0⟩⟨0| → |1⟩⟨1|) — diagonal density matrices; this covers all existing src/ callers (library/patterns.jl Grover diffusion, block_encoding/prepare.jl+select.jl ancillas, control/cases.jl targets). (2) For logical X_L on CSS self-dual codes like Steane, X^⊗7 and Y^⊗7 both flip |0⟩_L ↔ |1⟩_L. So the existing qecc X_L test passes for either convention. (3) Grover's diffusion operator H-X-(flip)-X-H applies X! AFTER H, where the qubit is in |+⟩ — this is where the bug could manifest, but test_grover currently passes (need to audit why — likely coincidence).

Discovery: bead 870 P1 syndrome-value tests (asserting sx==qubit_index, sz==0 for an injected 'X error') failed because injecting X!(q) was injecting Y, which X-stabs detect as Z-component AND Z-stabs detect as X-component → both syndromes nonzero.

Fix: swap the two definitions in src/gates.jl — X!(q) = (q.φ += π; q.θ += π; q) and Y!(q) = (q.θ += π; q). Channel-level blast radius: near-zero for the freshly-|0⟩ ancilla sites (identical channels); must verify test_grover still passes (superposition interference is at risk).

Acceptance: (a) X!(|+⟩) → |+⟩ (invariant), Y!(|+⟩) → |-⟩ (with measurement); (b) full test suite regression-clean after swap; (c) decouple from bead 870 — 870 resumes using corrected X!/Y! and its P1 syndrome-value assertions become green.

title: Coset representation of modular integers (Zalka 1998, GE21 §2.4)
description: Tier-1 GE21 optimisation. Coset representation stores k (mod N) as the periodic superposition (2^-c_pad)^½ Σ_{j=0..2^c_pad-1} |jN+k⟩ on a register with c_pad = O(lg n) extra high-order qubits. Non-modular (plain) adders then approximately reduce modulo N automatically via periodicity; error is exponentially suppressed in c_pad. This eliminates the expensive modular-reduction step of Beauregard's modadd (which costs ~10n Toffolis per add for comparison + conditional subtract); replacement is a plain ripple or QFT adder (~4n Toffolis). Reduces leading Toffoli term from 20·n_e·n² to 8·n_e·n². Scope: (a) new src/library/patterns.jl::coset_encode!(q::QInt{W}, N::Int; c_pad::Int) and coset_decode! inverse pair; (b) add_plain_qft!(y::QInt{W+c_pad}, a::Int) non-modular variant of add_qft!; (c) error analysis of coset vs exact modular state; (d) tests showing coset-encoded add stays within approximation error bound. title: Semi-classical iQFT for shor_order_D (Beauregard §2.4 Fig. 8, one-controlling-qubit trick)
description:
Beauregard 2003 §2.4 (pp. 8-9, Fig. 8) shows that the t counter qubits in Shor order-finding can be replaced by a **single recycled qubit** plus semi-classical inverse QFT. Each iteration i = 0, …, t-1:

  1. Hadamard the single counter qubit (|0⟩ → |+⟩)
  2. Apply a classical-feedback R_{2i} phase gate on the counter qubit, where the phase is a function of all prior measurement outcomes m_0, …, m_{i-1} (the paper's eq. in Fig. 8 caption)
  3. Controlled-U^{2^i} on the y register (our `mulmod_beauregard!`)
  4. Hadamard the counter qubit
  5. Measure it as m_i
  6. X^{m_i} on the next round's counter prep (absorbed into the classical R_{2i} computation)

The c-U gates all commute, and the inverse QFT can be applied semi-classically (measurement-driven) because each measured bit dictates a unitary correction applied after the next c-U^{2^i} step.

Result: **HWM drops from t + 2L + 3 to 1 + 2L + 3 = 2L + 4** total qubits. At L=14, HWM drops from 59 to 32 — fits Orkan's 30-qubit cap. At L=18, 40 qubits — still too big for Orkan, but matches Beauregard's titular '2n+3 qubits' bound exactly.

Implementation: new `shor_order_D_semi(a, N; t)` (or add `semi_classical=true` kwarg to shor_order_D). Uses `Bool(q)` casts (P2 measurement) + ClassicalRef to accumulate prior-measurement state; each R_{2i} phase is computed classically from the measurement log.

Acceptance:
- `shor_order_D_semi(a, N; t)` implemented.
- Correctness verified on N=15, N=21, N=35 — hit rates match shor_order_D (within ±5% on 30-shot samples).
- HWM measured = 2L + 4 at peak (verify via ctx.n_qubits, not ctx.capacity).
- Classical R_{2i} helper + docstring cites Beauregard §2.4 Fig. 8 and docs/physics/beauregard_2003_2n3_shor.pdf.
- Simulation runnable up to L≥12 on Orkan (where shor_order_D hits the 30-qubit cap).
- No change to mulmod_beauregard! (keep the uf4 signature stable).

Unblocks: L≥10 end-to-end simulation of Shor on Orkan. Does NOT affect DAG-level scaling (bench_shor_scaling.jl traces stay polynomial either way). This is a simulator-ceiling unblocker, not a scaling change.

title: Controlled classical-constant modular multiplier: mulmod_beauregard!(y::QInt{L}, a::Int, N::Int, ctrl)
description:
Implement controlled quantum register multiplication by a classical constant mod N, following Beauregard 2003 Fig. 6. This is the workhorse that replaces QROM-based mulmod in impls A/B/C.

Structure:
  controlled_mulmod(a, N, ctrl, x) computes: if ctrl then x := (a*x) mod N else x unchanged.
  Implementation: for each bit j of x (from LSB), controlled-modadd(y, (a * 2^j) mod N, N, ctrl AND x[j]).
  Uses an accumulator ancilla y initialized to 0, then SWAP the final y with x, then uncompute y using the inverse mulmod (a^{-1} mod N).

So: L calls to modadd! with different constants (a, 2a mod N, 4a mod N, ...) + SWAP + L inverse modadds with a^{-1} constants.

Classical constants a_j = a·2^j mod N are precomputed (same pattern as impl C's a_js line 733-738 in src/library/shor.jl). Inverse a^{-1} mod N computed via extended Euclidean (Julia's invmod). gcd(a, N) must be 1 — already guaranteed by impl C's parent context.

Depends on Sturm.jl-dgy (modadd!). Total gates: O(L) modadd! calls · O(L²) gates each = O(L³) total. Matches Beauregard 2003 quote: '2n+3 qubits, O(n³) gates'.

Acceptance: mulmod_beauregard!(x, a, N, ctrl) on x::QInt{L} quantum, (a, N) classical. Verified on all (a, N, x) with L=4, gcd(a,N)=1. Controlled variant coherent. Gate count scales as L³, verified at L=4,5,6 showing polynomial (not exponential) growth.

title: Classical-constant modular adder: modadd!(y::QInt{L}, a::Int, N::Int, ctrl)
description:
Implement controlled modular addition y ↦ (y + a) mod N for quantum y and classical a, N. This is Beauregard 2003 Fig. 5 — the second building block after the QFT-adder.

Structure (Beauregard 2003 §3.3):
  1. Add a to y using add_qft! (ancilla register in Fourier basis).
  2. Subtract N (also via add_qft! with -N).
  3. Check MSB (comparator): if MSB=1, the subtraction underflowed → need to add N back.
  4. Add N conditionally (controlled on the MSB check).
  5. Subtract a, re-add a (uncompute the check) — Beauregard's comparator uncompute.

Requires a comparator qubit (one ancillary qubit that holds the MSB sign, reset after use). Control input is a classical boolean or quantum bit — when called from mulmod, it will be a quantum ctrl.

Depends on Sturm.jl-ar7 (QFT-adder). The overall logic is 5 calls to add_qft! + one ancilla + classical glue. Total O(L²) gates.

Acceptance: modadd!(y::QInt{L}, a::Int, N::Int) computes y := (y + a) mod N. Verified against all (L,a,N,y) with L=4, 0<=a,y<N, N=5..15 — that's < 2000 cases, fully deterministic test. Controlled variant modadd!(y, a, N, ctrl::QBool) leaves y unchanged when ctrl=0 and performs the update when ctrl=1 (Bell-pair superposition test confirms coherence).

title: QFT-adder (Draper 2000): add_qft!(y::QInt{L}, a::Int)
description:
Implement the Draper quantum Fourier-transform adder as a Sturm library function in src/library/arithmetic.jl (or similar). This is the foundational primitive for Beauregard mulmod — polynomial in L, no ancillae.

The Draper adder acts on L qubits in Fourier basis: after QFT, each qubit j accumulates phase proportional to the classical constant's j-th bit. So QFT → controlled phase rotations → QFT† implements y ↦ y + a mod 2^L on a quantum register y using only 4 Sturm primitives (Rz for phase, and the QFT itself which is already in src/library/patterns.jl as fourier_sample's inverse).

Gate count: O(L²) Rz + 2·QFT (O(L²) gates). Physics: see Draper 2000 (quant-ph/0008033) — download to docs/physics/ if not already there. Beauregard 2003 uses this as Fig. 2.

title: EPIC — Polynomial-in-L Shor via Beauregard arithmetic mulmod (shor_order_D)
description:
Existing Shor impls A/B/C all use QROM-based modular multiplication and scale exponentially in L: A=O(L·4^L), B=O(L·2^{3L}), C=O(L²·2^L). Measured at L=8: A=1.1M gates, B=672M gates, C=328k gates. For useful crypto (L=1024) any of these needs >10^30 gates. This is a DEAD END for Shor at useful scales.

Total: O(L³) Toffoli, 2L+3 qubits. Häner-Roetteler-Svore 2016 achieves O(L² log L) with QCLA. Gidney-Ekerå 2021 prove real-world feasibility at ~3·10⁹ Toffolis for RSA-2048.

title: P9 auto-dispatch: f(q) falls through to oracle(f,q) via generated fallback
description: Implement the P9 axiom's core requirement: calling a classical Julia function f on a Quantum argument must automatically lower to oracle(f, q) without user-visible syntax. At compile time, inspect hasmethod(f, classical_types_of(args)); if a classical method exists, lower to oracle(f, args...); else raise MethodError. Must NOT be method piracy (scope via Quantum ABC). Must NOT shadow user overloads on quantum types (dispatch specificity wins). Cache on (f, argtypes) keyed alongside quantum(f). Reference: ForwardDiff.Dual / Enzyme.gradient patterns. Acceptance: f(x::Int8)=x^2+3x+1; f(QInt{8}(...)) works without wrapping, produces same circuit as oracle(f, x).
design: Generated fallback on <:Quantum types. hasmethod(f, classical_ts) at compile time. oracle(f, args...) lowering. Shared cache with quantum(f). Method-piracy-safe: scoped to types we own.
acceptance_criteria: f(q) works for any classical f defined on Int/Int8/..../Float64 when called with corresponding QInt{W}; identical circuit to oracle(f, q); user overloads win by specificity; works inside when() with auto-controlled lift

Landed in partial form (15/15 tests): abstract type Quantum, QBool/QInt<:Quantum, classical_type + classical_compile_kwargs traits, _P9_CACHE/clear_auto_cache! infrastructure. title: QSVT phase_factors: rhw_factorize O(n³) → Levinson-Durbin O(n log² n) upgrade
description:
P1 from 2026-04-27 review (area3).

src/qsvt/phase_factors.jl rhw_factorize uses O(n³) dense `A \\ rhs`. Documented inline as temporary but no bead tracks the upgrade. For QSVT polynomials of moderate degree (n>200) this is the dominant cost.

## Fix
Replace with Levinson-Durbin O(n log² n) recursion (standard for Toeplitz systems).

## Refs
- area3 finding P1 (qsvt/phase_factors)
notes:
Investigation 2026-05-03: scope sharpened.

The 2m×2m system is NOT plain Toeplitz — it's a 2x2 block matrix [I, -T^T; T*, I] where T_k is m×m Toeplitz. Standard Levinson-Durbin does not apply directly.

Block-elimination reduces to: (I + T_k·T_k*)·ã = rev(e_0), which is m×m Hermitian PSD. But (I + T·T*) is **displacement-rank ≤ 4**, NOT Toeplitz. Levinson-Durbin proper is O(n²) for plain Toeplitz; getting O(n²) on displacement-structured matrices needs the Schur algorithm; getting O(n log² n) needs Ammar-Gragg 1988 (or Bitmead-Anderson 1980 displacement-rank superfast).

Empirical scaling (2026-05-03, OMP=16):
  d=16  (n=32):     66 ms
  d=32  (n=64):    180 ms (2.7x)
  d=64  (n=128):   657 ms (3.7x)
  d=128 (n=256):  1166 ms (1.8x)
Effective scaling ~O(n^2.5)–O(n^3) thanks to BLAS-tuned LU. Pre-existing comment 'documented inline as temporary' overstates the cost — at d=200 the call is ~3s, not the 'dominant cost'.

## Refined three-phase plan

**Phase A** — Block elimination + dense O(m²) memory (mechanical, ~50 LOC):
Reduce 2m×2m to m×m Hermitian PSD: (I + T·T*)·ã = rev(e_0). Solve with cholesky! / ldlt!. Saves a 8x constant-factor and halves the memory; same O(m³) per-system asymptotic.

**Phase B** — Schur algorithm on displacement-rank-4 matrix (~200 LOC, careful numerics):
Per-system O(m²); total O(n³). Ref: Heinig & Rost 1984 'Algebraic Methods for Toeplitz-like Matrices and Operators'. Need stability tests against the dense baseline.

**Phase C** — Ammar-Gragg superfast (asymptotic O(m log² m); only worth it for d > 500-ish):
Bead's original 'O(n log² n)' target. Significant implementation effort; numerically delicate. Defer until a concrete d ≥ 500 use case lands.

## Acceptance (revised)

- Phase A as a P2 mechanical commit.
- Phase B as a separate P2 with regression tests against the dense baseline at d ∈ {16, 32, 64, 128}: max |F_dense - F_schur| < 1e-9.
- Phase C only if a real workload demands it.

Bead retitled implicitly via this note. Demoting from P1 to P2 at the same time — actual user impact is moderate; not blocking any in-flight work.

title: Perf: _shor_mulmod_E_controlled! at N=15 takes ~21 min per call
description:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-04-25 (supersedes original hypothesis).

Original hypothesis (workspace alloc/dealloc in `_multi_controlled_gate!`) is WRONG. Empirically: workspace pool saves only ~50 ms of 1260 s = 0.04%. See `bd memories sturm-jl-059-root-cause-confirmed-2026-04`.

REAL BOTTLENECK: `EagerContext.n_qubits` and the Orkan state grow monotonically and never shrink. Bennett ancilla allocations during `apply_reversible!` (and other transient allocations) ratchet `n_qubits` upward. After ancillae are deallocated, slots are returned to `free_slots` but `n_qubits` stays at peak. Every subsequent Orkan gate operates on `2^n_qubits` amplitudes — even when only 6-7 wires are actually live.

Empirical impact (probes in repo root, see WORKLOG):
  * N=7 c_mul=1 mulmod: 14.5 s wall. End-state live=6 but n_qubits=22 (state stays 2^22 = 4M amps). Compact layout would be 2^6 = 64 amps. ~290x slowdown vs ideal.
  * N=15 c_mul=1 mulmod: 378 s = 6.3 min wall. End live=7, n_qubits=26 (2^26 = 67M amps). ~280x slowdown vs ideal.
  * N=15 c_mul=2 mulmod: ~21 min consistent with one extra qubit of peak.
  * Per-call growth: controlled `add_qft_quantum!` is 4 ms at 15 live, 41 ms at 18 live, 12,000 ms at 25 live.

FIX SCOPE: state-compaction primitive `compact_state!(ctx)` that
  (1) builds a permutation from current live slot indices to compact 0..k-1 layout,
  (2) reads old amplitudes via `unsafe_wrap`, writes to a smaller Orkan state via the live-bit-mask scheme (relies on freed slots being |0> — currently guaranteed by `measure!` in deallocate path),
  (3) swaps in the new state, decrements n_qubits/capacity, remaps wire_to_qubit, clears free_slots.

Soundness: freed slots are guaranteed |0> by `_blessed_measure!` reset path (eager.jl:267-275), so the state factorises as |psi_live> tensor |0...0>_freed. Compaction extracts the |psi_live> factor exactly.

Trigger: opportunistic, fired when `length(free_slots) / n_qubits` exceeds a threshold OR when `allocate!` would trigger `_grow_state!` (try compact first, then grow if still needed).

DENSE/TRACE/HARDWARE: each context kind needs its own compact_state! (or no-op for TracingContext). Density matrix compaction is more expensive (2^n x 2^n) but follows the same principle.

This is a CORE change (touches `src/context/eager.jl` and the Orkan FFI surface). Per CLAUDE.md rule 2: 3+1 agents required (2 proposers + 1 implementer + orchestrator-as-reviewer). Spec lives in this bead; sub-tasks tracked as follow-on beads.

Probes used to converge: probe_mc_dealloc_cost.jl, probe_qrom_cold.jl, probe_add_qft_isolated.jl, probe_peak_qubits.jl, probe_mulmod_phases.jl. All in repo root.
design:
=== compact_state! design (research-backed, 2026-04-25) ===

CONTRACT:
  Pre  - no gate ccall in flight (between-operations only).
       - all free_slots were freed via _blessed_measure! (deterministic |0>).
       - Σ|amps[i+1]|² over i with (i & freed_bit_mask) != 0  <  tolerance.
  Post - wire_to_qubit maps each live wire to slot 0..k-1 (k = live count).
       - n_qubits = k, capacity = k + GROW_STEP hysteresis.
       - free_slots = [].
       - ctx.orkan is fresh OrkanState(ORKAN_PURE, capacity), |0>-projected
         and permuted from old buffer.
       - subsequent statistics identical mod global phase.
  Violation: error() loud, name the residual norm² for diagnosis.

MECHANISM (Julia-only, no new Orkan FFI):
  1. live_wires = sort!(collect(keys(wire_to_qubit)), by=w->w.id).
  2. old_slots = sort!([wire_to_qubit[w] for w in live_wires]).
  3. STURM_COMPACT_VERIFY: scan residual norm; error if > 1e-12 · 2^n_freed.
  4. new_orkan = OrkanState(ORKAN_PURE, new_n + hysteresis).
  5. Scatter copy via unsafe_wrap: for j in 0..2^new_n - 1, decode j into
     bits, insert each bit k at old_slots[k+1] in old index i, copy
     new_amps[j+1] = old_amps[i+1]. O(2^new_n · new_n).
  6. Install new orkan, capacity, n_qubits; rebuild wire_to_qubit; clear
     free_slots. Old OrkanState GC'd via finalizer.

TRIGGER POLICY (default just-before-grow):
  - manual: compact_state!(ctx) callable.
  - threshold-auto: opt-in via kwarg.
  - just-before-grow (DEFAULT): allocate! tries compact_state! before
    _grow_state!; skips grow if post-compact n_qubits < capacity.

PRIOR ART: novel runtime primitive. Aer/qsim/IQS/CUDA-Q/TKET all keep
2^n vector after measurement; qubit reuse is universally a compile-time
rewrite. Closest runtime ref: arXiv:2410.04252 (Lazy Qubit Reordering)
for bit-permutation mechanics.

NON-EAGER CONTEXTS:
  - TracingContext: no Orkan state → no-op (live::Vector is already
    insertion-ordered).
  - HardwareContext: no client-side Orkan → no-op + warn-once. Server-
    side _SimSession.eager compacts independently; insulated from
    device-ABI by the qubit_to_wire indirection.
  - DensityMatrixContext: separate bead (2D row+col permutation).

INVARIANT/TEST CALL SITES TO TOUCH:

    growth; rewrite to use a peak-watermark callback inside the op.

    rewrite to test "ancillae returned" rather than "free_slots length".

title: QROM measurement-based O(√L) uncomputation — Gidney 2019 Fig 3
description:
Phase D3 of 6oc: replace the second qrom_lookup_xor! in _pep_mod_iter! with measurement-based uncomputation. Cost drops from 2·(2^c − 1) Toffoli per lookup-pair to ⌈2^c / k⌉ + k (optimum 2·√(2^c) at k ≈ √(2^c)). At c_mul=5 / d=32 / k=4: 12 vs 62 (~80% saving). Unblocks bead 6oc criterion (d) Toffoli-count bench at L=8.

GROUND TRUTH: Berry, Gidney, Motta, McClean, Babbush (2019) 'Qubitization of arbitrary basis quantum chemistry leveraging sparsity and low rank factorization', arXiv:1902.02134, **Appendix C, Theorem 3 (Eq. 67), Figs 5-8**. Local: docs/physics/berry_gidney_motta_mcclean_babbush_2019_qubitization.pdf. GE21 §2.5 cites this paper as [8] for MBU.

CONSTRUCTION (Fig 6, clean ancillae):
1. X-basis measure the output register. Outcomes m ∈ {0,1}^M.
2. Classically determine S = {x : parity(m · T[x]) = 1}, the set of addr states to phase-flip.
3. Apply phase fixup via clean ancillae:
   a. Alloc k clean ancillae (k = next_pow2(ceil(sqrt(2^Win)))).
   b. X on anc[0]; controlled-swap cascade (Fig 8, _binary_to_unary!) shifts the |1⟩ to position indexed by addr[low log k bits], producing a one-hot encoding.
   c. H on each ancilla.
   d. Standard XOR-table-lookup (qrom_lookup_xor!) on addr[high bits] targeting the k unary ancillae, with the classically-precomputed fixup table that negates phases of states in S.
   e. H on each ancilla.
   f. Reverse controlled-swap cascade.
   g. X on anc[0]; release.

Key simplification: step (d) REUSES the existing qrom_lookup_xor! primitive — only one new helper, _binary_to_unary!, is needed. No separate 'phase-only QROM' needed.

SIGNATURE: qrom_lookup_uncompute_meas!(scratch::QInt{Wtot}, addr::QInt{Win}, tbl::QROMTable{Win,Wtot}). Consumes scratch (measures it out), leaves addr correctly phased (i.e., scratch went from |T[addr]⟩ to ⟨0| via MBU).

STAGED DELIVERY: bvq (grounding, closing), 123 (_binary_to_unary! + sub-primitive tests), 1q9 (qrom_lookup_uncompute_meas! + unit tests), 7cl (mbu kwarg on plus_equal_product_mod!), 4hz (bench + close 6oc (d)).
design: Protocol (Gidney 2019 §2 text + Fig 3): (1) X-basis measure scratch → classical m; (2) address register has picked up phase (-1)^(m · T[addr]); (3) apply Z on a 1-bit scratch computed via small QROM over the split-address representation — binary-to-unary conversion on low-half a_0 (Fig 4, Fredkin gates, cost ~2^{ceil(W_in/2)}), high-half fixup lookup targeting low-half (cost ~2^{floor(W_in/2)}). Total O(√L) Toffoli. Builds on the existing qrom_lookup_xor! primitive by using it with a smaller classical fixup table. Signature: qrom_lookup_uncompute_meas!(scratch::QInt, addr::QInt, table::QROMTable). Consumes scratch (measures it out); leaves addr correctly phased.

title: [SPECULATIVE] TracingContext: if Bool(q) auto-captures both branches via speculative-execution tracer
description:
**STATUS: SPECULATIVE — design discussion not concluded.** User remains "somehow unhappy" with the proposed sentinel-throw-and-replay approach. File this so we can return to it; do NOT start implementation without resuming the design conversation.

**Problem.** TracingContext (DAG IR) is supposed to be a DAG that holds *both* branches of a quantum-conditioned classical `if`, so the emitted OpenQASM/IR contains a CasesNode and downstream passes can reason about both arms. The IR supports this — `CasesNode{true_branch, false_branch}` already exists, and the `cases()` primitive (Sturm.jl-322 / -tak fixes) lets the user opt in explicitly. But the natural Julia syntax `if Bool(q) … else … end` cannot work today: `Bool(q)` in TracingContext has nothing meaningful to return — it has to give Julia *one* concrete boolean for the host `if` to branch on, and whichever it picks, only one arm gets traced into the DAG.

The user's intuition: "the TracingContext DAG should literally contain both branches" — which IS what the IR allows. The gap is purely in the frontend tracer.

**Proposed design (the one user agreed-with-reservations).** Speculative execution / branch oracle, JAX `lax.cond` analogue:

1. `Bool(q)` in TracingContext returns a sentinel `TraceBool` value. Using it in `if` (i.e. converting to `Bool`) throws a typed exception `SpeculativeBranchSentinel(branch_point_id)`.
2. The trace driver wraps the user function in a `try/catch`. On sentinel: replay `f` from the start with a *branch oracle* that forces this branch point to `true`; replay again forcing `false`; recursively handle nested branches (2^k replays for k measurements).
3. After all replays, merge the sub-DAGs into a `CasesNode` at the original branch point.

**Constraints / open issues that fuel the unhappiness.**
- **Purity required.** Replay only works if `f` has no side effects outside the DAG. Need side-effect detection (or a purity contract the user opts into).
- **Deterministic WireID allocation across replays.** Same lexical wire allocation site must produce the same WireID on every replay, otherwise sub-DAGs can't be merged. Likely needs an allocator keyed by (caller location, replay-local counter) rather than a global atomic.
- **Loops with measurements explode.** k measurements × n loop iterations ⇒ 2^(k·n) replays. Need a bounded-replay budget with a clear error when exceeded; user falls back to explicit `cases()` / `while_loop()`.
- **Exception-as-control-flow smell.** Throwing through user code to drive the tracer is dirty; alternatives include source-level rewriting (Cassette.jl / IRTools.jl) or a macro-driven CPS transform. None are obviously better. *This is part of why user is uneasy.*
- **Composability with `when()`** (coherent control) and with `oracle()` (Bennett reversible-circuit lift): the three branching constructs (`if` after measurement → speculative-trace; `when` → coherent control; `if` inside `oracle` → Bennett reversible branch) must remain syntactically distinct or P4 is violated. Need to confirm the sentinel approach doesn't accidentally collapse them.

**Why not just use cases().** `cases()` is the explicit-path workaround (already shipped via 322/tak). It's good as fallback but it forces the user to write `cases(q) do … end` instead of plain `if Bool(q) … end`, which is the kind of boilerplate P1 (functions are channels) is meant to eliminate.

**Status.** Speculative. Design conversation paused mid-flight on session 38 (commit 80fdcdb, 2026-04-21). Resume by re-reading the design above and re-engaging the open issues — especially the exception-as-control-flow smell and whether IRTools-style rewriting would be cleaner.
design: Sentinel-throw on Bool(q) in TracingContext + branch-oracle replay + CasesNode merge. JAX lax.cond analogue. Open alternatives: source rewriting (Cassette/IRTools), CPS transform via macro. Constraints: purity, deterministic WireID across replays, bounded replay count for loops, must remain distinct from when() and oracle().
notes: SPECULATIVE — do NOT implement. User explicitly noted they 'remain somehow unhappy' with the agreed direction. Resume the design conversation before any code. Cross-reference: cases() primitive (closed Sturm.jl-322, Sturm.jl-tak) is the explicit-path fallback this would supersede for the if Bool(q) case.

title: shor_factor_EH_semi — Mosca-Ekert semi-classical iQFT for two-register EH17
description: Current shor_factor_EH (bead 6bn, commit 6e0cc60) uses full two-register PE: first_reg(ℓ+m) + second_reg(ℓ) + y_reg(L) = 2ℓ+m+L steady-state, peak 2ℓ+m+2L+3 = 24 qubits at N=55. Mosca-Ekert (1999) describes a semi-classical iQFT adaptation for multi-register DLP that collapses each exponent register to a SINGLE recycled QBool (same trick Beauregard 2003 applied to Shor order-finding in shor_order_D_semi). Goal: shor_factor_EH_semi(N) with peak ≈ L+5 instead of 2ℓ+m+L+5. For N=15: 19 → ~9 qubits. For N=55: 24 → ~13 qubits. Enables toy-N multi-shot testing that's currently infeasible (6bn's N=55 demo took 13m16s/shot at full width).
design: Two semi-classical iQFT loops, one per register, with cross-register classical phase correction. RESEARCH STEP required: session 36 notes explicitly found 'EH17 is NOT directly amenable to Griffiths-Niu semi-classical iQFT' because the (j,k) correlation is joint via shared e=a-bd. Mosca-Ekert §3.2 supposedly solves this but the exact phase-correction formula is NOT obvious from EH17 alone. Phase 0: read Mosca-Ekert 1999 §3 AND work out the phase accumulator recurrence on paper before coding. Phase 1: implement shor_factor_EH_semi mirroring shor_order_D_semi's outer structure: two fresh QBool c_a, c_b per exp-bit, H!, classical correction, controlled mulmod, H!, measure. Phase 2: verify on N=15 against shor_factor_EH hit rate. Phase 3: scale to N=55 and confirm peak ≤ 13 qubits.
acceptance_criteria: (a) shor_factor_EH_semi(15) returns Set([3,5]) ≥ 50% over 30 shots (matches 6bn acceptance). (b) Peak qubit count via TracingContext: shor_factor_EH_semi(15) ≤ shor_factor_EH(15) - 5. (c) shor_factor_EH_semi(55; m=3, ell=3) peak ≤ 13 qubits (vs 24 for full version). (d) shor_factor_EH_semi(55) single-shot runtime ≤ 30s (vs 13m16s for full version) — unlocks multi-shot test feasibility at N=55. (e) Documented phase-correction derivation in a code comment + docs/physics link to Mosca-Ekert paper (needs to be fetched first — file as blocker if paper not locally available).
notes: Refs: Mosca, Ekert. 'The Hidden Subgroup Problem and Eigenvalue Estimation on a Quantum Computer.' NASA QCQC 1999, Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol 1509, pp. 174-188. EH17 §4.7 references this as [4]. Also Griffiths-Niu 1996 (quant-ph/9511007) and Parker-Plenio 2000 (quant-ph/0001104) §II for single-register semi-classical. PDF to fetch: https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9903071 (Mosca-Ekert preprint). Session 36 WORKLOG explicitly notes 'EH17's §4.3 is NOT directly semi-classical-izable' and flags Mosca-Ekert as the adapted form. 6bn's 9-qubit exponent cost at N=15 is therefore REDUCIBLE — this bead delivers that reduction.

title: shor_factor_EH s>1 — multi-shot lattice post-processing (EH17 §4.4 general)
description: Current shor_factor_EH implements s=1 only (single-shot classical post-processing, 2D Lagrange). EH17 §4.2–§4.4 generalizes to s ≥ 1: collecting s good pairs {(j_1,k_1),...,(j_s,k_s)} and solving an (s+1)-dimensional lattice CVP to extract d. At s>1 exponent-register total width shrinks from 2ℓ+m ≈ 1.5n (s=1) asymptotically toward (1/2 + 1/s)·n — i.e., ~0.5n for large s. This is the entire point of the 2017 generalization over Ekerå 2016's s=1 algorithm. Filed as a follow-on to Sturm.jl-6bn (shipped 2026-04-20, commit 6e0cc60).
design: Add kwarg s::Int=1 to shor_factor_EH. For s>1: (a) run quantum step s times sequentially, collecting (j_i, k_i); (b) construct the s-dim lattice L per EH17 Def 3 with basis rows [[j_1,...,j_s,1], [2^(ℓ+m),0,...,0], ..., [0,...,0,2^(ℓ+m),0]]; (c) solve CVP via 2D Lagrange (s=1 reuses _eh_recover_d_candidates) or LLL+Babai for s≥2 (~200 lines pure Julia); (d) verify each candidate d via _eh_factors_from_d. Per EH17 §4.4 Lemma 3, spurious short-vector probability drops to 2^(-s-1) so s=2 already halves ambiguity over s=1.
acceptance_criteria: shor_factor_EH(15; s=2) returns Set([3,5]) ≥ 50% over 30 shots (collecting 2 good pairs per attempt). shor_factor_EH(15; s=3) ≥ 60%. s=1 path unchanged from 6bn. New test file test_eh_s_gt_1.jl with LLL unit tests against reference vectors (e.g. the [[5,3],[1,3]] basis reduces to [[1,3],[2,-3]]) and end-to-end multi-shot run.
notes: EH17 §4.4 Def 3 lattice; Lemma 3 spurious-vector bound 2^(-s-1); Theorem 1 conservative 2^(-3) per-shot good-pair probability. For production s>1, fpLLL_jll or Nemo.jl could be optional deps via Pkg extras — but start with pure-Julia LLL (Lenstra-Lenstra-Lovász 1982 with δ=3/4; ~200 lines). Related: Gidney-Ekerå 2021 §2.1 uses s=1 in the RSA-2048 analysis — s>1 is more relevant for larger crypto sizes. Ground truth: docs/physics/ekera_2017_short_dlp.pdf §4.2–§4.4.

title: QRunway runway-in-middle layout: high part above runway (Theorem 4.2 active)

title: shor_factor_EH — Ekerå-Håstad 2017 short-DLP derivative
description: Tier-1 GE21 optimisation. Ekerå-Håstad 2017 derivative of Shor factors N=pq by computing the short discrete logarithm d = log_g(g^{N+1}) mod r where g is random in Z_N*. Uses two exponent registers e_1 (length 2m) and e_2 (length m) where m ≈ 0.5n + O(1), for total n_e = 1.5n vs Shor's 2n — ~25% fewer controlled modular multiplications. Classical post-processing uses lattice reduction (Babai / LLL) to extract d, then p,q as roots of quadratic p²-dp+N=0. Scope: (a) new src/library/shor.jl::shor_factor_EH(N; max_attempts=16); (b) two-register phase estimation with interleaved controlled mulmod by random g; (c) classical post-processing (lattice reduction — may use Hermite basis reduction or simple rational reconstruction); (d) tests on N=15 (n=4, m=3, n_e=6), N=21 (n=5, m=3, n_e=8). Ground truth: docs/physics/ — need to fetch Ekerå 2017 (arxiv 1702.00249), Ekerå-Håstad 2017 (arxiv 1707.08494); GE21 §2.1.
design: Two-register PE: initialize e_1=|+⟩^{2m}, e_2=|+⟩^m; apply f(e_1,e_2) = g^{e_1} · y^{-e_2} where y = g^{N+1}. QFT e_1 and e_2 independently. Measure. Classical lattice post-processing extracts d = log_g(y) mod r ≈ p+q. Given d+N=pq → p,q roots of quadratic.
acceptance_criteria: shor_factor_EH(15) returns Set([3,5]) ≥50% over 30 shots. Per-shot mulmod count = n_e = 1.5n = 6 for n=4 (vs 8 for impl D at n=4). Traces validate n_e=1.5n scaling. Falls back gracefully when lattice reconstruction fails.
notes:
Research round 2026-04-20 (session 35). Refs: docs/physics/ekera_2017_short_dlp.pdf (arXiv:1702.00249 — THIS is the actual Ekerå-Håstad 2017 paper despite filename, verified by reading title page 2026-04-20); ekera_2023_single_run_dlp.pdf (arXiv:2309.01754); gidney_ekera_2021_rsa2048.pdf §2.1.

CORRECTION — earlier ekera_hastad_2017_n_plus_half_n.pdf was a misfiled building-energy paper; deleted in preflight (bead rqg).

GROUND TRUTH — short-DLP (EH17 §4.3): function f(a,b) = [a-bd]g. For RSA factoring (EH17 §5.2), g random coprime, y = g^{(N+1)} mod N (GE21 normalisation) or g^{(N-1)/2} (EH17 normalisation). Secret d = p+q (GE21) or (p+q-2)/2 (EH17).

TWO REGISTERS — register 1: 2m qubits (e_1), register 2: m qubits (e_2). Total n_e = 3m ≈ 1.5n+O(1) vs Shor's 2n. GE21 uses s=1 (ℓ=m).

POST-PROCESSING — for s=1 (GE21 default): 2D lattice, CLOSED-FORM via Lagrange reduction (equivalent to 2D extended Euclidean). NO Hecke.jl or Nemo.jl dep needed — ~20 lines pure Julia, mirrors _shor_convergents. For s>1 BKZ blocksize min(10,s+1) via fpLLL — defer.

FACTOR RECOVERY — trivial quadratic: p,q roots of x²-dx+N=0. Julia: isqrt(d²-4N) + primality check.

SUCCESS PROB — EH17 Theorem 1: ≥1/8 per single shot (conservative). Ekerå 2023: >99% at large m with Lagrange. At small m (N=15): empirical 50-90%.

TESTS — small N multi-shot: shor_factor_EH(15) across 200 shots, accept if (3,5) returned ≥ 40%. Multi-shot aggregation (8 outputs, majority vote) raises to 0.9+.

INDEPENDENT AT CIRCUIT LEVEL — can land anytime after D_semi. For GE21 cost match would need 6oc underneath, but driver itself does not need coset/runway/windowed to be functional.

title: Oblivious carry runways (Gidney 2019, GE21 §2.6)
description: Tier-1 GE21 optimisation. Oblivious carry runways insert a runway qubit at some position p in a register, and terminate the carry propagation of a ripple adder into it. This splits an n-bit addition into parallelisable pieces of size n/c_sep each; carry-signal-removal is classical post-measurement. Nearly halves addition depth at <1% qubit overhead. Scope: (a) src/library/patterns.jl::insert_runway!(y::QInt{W}, p::Int) / remove_runway! primitive pair; (b) add_ripple_runway! using Cuccaro's ripple adder with runway termination; (c) tests showing runway-augmented add matches plain add within ε=2^-c_pad for c_sep runway spacing. Does NOT plug into Shor in this bead (follow-up combines with coset). Ground truth: docs/physics/gidney_ekera_2021_rsa2048.pdf §2.6 + Gidney 2019 'Approximate encoded permutations' (arxiv 1905.08488) — need to fetch.
design: Runway qubit initialised to |+⟩ absorbs carry bits via CNOT; at end it holds the carry-out signal in superposition. Classical runway removal: measure runway, XOR into next-block MSB, classically track. GE21 points out runway removal can be deferred until just before the register is measured/discarded — post-processing not in superposition.
acceptance_criteria: add_ripple_runway!(y::QInt{8}, 13; c_sep=2) on y=QInt{8}(42) gives y=42+13=55 with error <2^-c_pad on all 2^W initial states. Depth reduction verified: depth(add_ripple_runway!) ~ n/c_sep vs n for plain ripple.
notes: Continuation of session 35 work after q84/8fy/6xi/amh chain. SCOPE NOTE: current QRunway{W, Cpad} (q84) puts runway at the HIGH END of reg (no high part above runway). Per Gidney Fig 2 analysis: with no high part, the |+⟩^Cpad runway is invariant under classical add of any constant (by superposition relabelling), so decoded low W bits = (v+a) mod 2^W deterministically — ZERO deviation. Theorem 4.2 deviation bound only kicks in with a high part above the runway (the runway-in-middle layout from Gidney Fig 2). For b3l minimum: ship runway_add! + runway_decode! + tests verifying decoded correctness. Multi-piece parallelism (the actual benefit per GE21 §2.6) deferred to follow-on; needs runway-in-middle config which is a different type signature.

title: Reconsider exporting compact_state! at public API surface (Pillar 4 seam)
description:
src/Sturm.jl:105 exports compact_state! at the public API. The
function is a statevector-specific performance knob (n_qubits ratchet,
free_slots compaction) — meaningful only on EagerContext /
DensityMatrixContext. On TracingContext, HardwareContext, and any
future tensor-network backend it is a documented no-op
(src/context/abstract.jl:223).

The abstract docstring at src/context/abstract.jl:174 also names

leaking into the abstract interface contract.

  (b) Move to a Sturm.Statevector submodule or trait; users call
      Sturm.Statevector.compact_state!(ctx) only when they know the

  (c) Make compaction fully transparent — internal triggers only,

The abstract docstring should be tightened regardless of which option

Pillar 4 leakage; not blocking but weakens the backend-agnostic
contract. Worth a deliberate decision before tensor-network or

title: Hand-rolled Babbush-Gidney unary iteration to bypass Bennett 4x QROM overhead
description: Sturm.jl-vbz closed 6oc(d) at L=8 to exactly 0.500× — TIGHT. The inner T table lookup in qrom_lookup_xor_cleanancilla! goes through Bennett-compiled qrom_lookup_xor!, which costs 4·(2^c − 1) Toffoli vs the 2^c − 1 the bare Babbush-Gidney unary iteration tree would cost (4× overhead). A hand-rolled unary-iteration primitive on the Sturm side would cut the App B forward cost by ~75% per lookup, pushing L=8 well below 0.5× and giving headroom on L ≥ 10. Scope: new src/library/qrom_unary.jl with a primitive that builds the unary iteration tree directly from 4 primitives + when() / _fredkin!, plus a kwarg or auto-dispatch on qrom_lookup_xor! to select between Bennett and unary modes. Ground truth: Babbush et al. 2018 arXiv:1805.03662 §III.C Fig 10 (already in docs/physics/babbush_2018_qrom_linear_T.pdf). Filed as vbz follow-on.

title: QMod{4} Ry — 6-Givens V4 decomposition (direct or sandwich)
description: Split from ixd (which shipped d=5 Ry via Euler sandwich). csw critical-path only needs d=3 and d=5; this is the d=4 follow-on. At d=4 (j=3/2, K=2, no leakage since power-of-2), the Wigner d^{3/2}(pi/3) matrix is 4x4 real orthogonal. Implementation options: (a) direct closed-form Givens decomposition of d^{3/2}(delta) — 6 adjacent Givens with delta-dependent angles, analogous to the k8u d=3 pattern (but without the leakage-state issue since K=2 exhausts 4 labels exactly); (b) Euler sandwich (same pattern as ixd d=5) with precomputed V4 = d^{3/2}(pi/2) fixed dressing. Proposer A (ixd review) suggested option (a) may beat (b) at d=4 because no leakage means no Hamming-scratch complexity, and 6 Givens < sandwich's 2*6 + 3 Rz overhead. Acceptance: d=4 q.theta+=pi/3 matches d^{3/2}(pi/3) column 0 numerically (use Julia matrix exp(-i delta J_y) as ground truth — do NOT rely on bead's formula if it disagrees with orchestrator numerics, same issue as ixd d=5). Full 5-col match. Subspace trivially preserved (no leakage). Mandatory pre-integration: orchestrator must numerically verify the 4x4 qubit unitary matches the target before shipping — k8u and ixd both had sign/precision bugs that would have been caught earlier with this rule. Refs: docs/design/k8u_design_{A,B}.md, docs/design/ixd_design_{A,B}.md, docs/physics/bartlett_deGuise_sanders_2002_qudit_simulation.pdf Eq. 5.

description: Bennett.jl currently lowers classical Julia functions to reversible circuits with mod-2^W arithmetic only. classical_type(::Type{<:QMod}) is intentionally not defined in bead 9aa, so oracle(f, q::QMod{d}) raises a MethodError. This bead extends Bennett.jl to support mod-d arithmetic (or QROM table fallback for arbitrary d) so QMod registers participate in the P9 oracle path. Until then, users wanting Bennett oracles use QBool/QInt only.

title: QECC module trait: restrict stabiliser codes to prime d
description: Current QECC module (src/qecc/) ships Steane [[7,1,3]] for qubits. At d>2 stabiliser codes require F_d field structure (Gottesman 1998 §2), field only for prime d. Add trait is_prime_d(d) used by AbstractCode dispatch; non-prime QMod{d} with QECC ops errors with pointer to goi-prime-power-galois. Priority: 3 — can defer past v0.1 qudit.

title: Formal Holstein-Primakoff derivation — qudit primitives to CV universal set
description: P7 CV correctness requires qudit primitive set to map to universal CV gate set at large d. Sketched in qudit_magic_gate_survey.md §5.5: Ry/Rz → x/p displacements, q.θ₂ (exp(-iδn̂²)) → Kerr, q.θ₃ (exp(-iδn̂³)) → GKP cubic-phase via Ry-conjugation. Rigorous derivation needed: (a) specify rescaling (J_±/√(2j) → a, a†?); (b) show primitive-generated Hamiltonians span {x, p, xp, x², x³} per Lloyd-Braunstein 1999 / Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill 2001 universal CV set; (c) quantify large-j error bound. Deliverable: docs/physics/qudit_cv_limit.md ≤500 lines. Non-blocking v0.1 but MUST settle before claiming P7 compliance.

title: Magic state distillation for composite d — literature gap
description: Literature gap from qudit_magic_gate_survey.md §4.3. For composite d (d=6, 10, 12, 14, 15, 21, …) no closed-form MSD protocol published. Natural approach is CRT factorisation (d=6 ≅ Z_2 × Z_3; run qubit MSD on 2-factor and qutrit MSD on 3-factor) but conflicts with user-level SUM mod d semantics. Prakash 2020 ternary Golay is d=3-specific; Anwar-Campbell-Browne 2012 is prime-specific. Research output: recommended protocol per d or documented no-go. Non-blocking v0.1.

title: Prime-power d via Galois-field F_{p^k} stabiliser formalism
description: Literature gap from qudit_magic_gate_survey.md §1.5. Gottesman 1998 §2 uses F_{p^k} (Galois field) rather than Z_{p^k} (modular arithmetic) for stabiliser codes at prime-power d (d=4, 8, 9, 16, 25, 27, 32). Sturm's QMod{d} currently implies modular Z_d arithmetic in SUM. Reconciliation requires structural rethink: (a) encode QMod{p^k} as k tensored QMod{p} via field representation; (b) add Galois-field SUM primitive distinct from modular SUM; (c) restrict QECC to strictly prime d, relegate p^k to separate QGalois{p,k} type. Non-blocking v0.1. Research bead.

title: Define T_d! for non-prime d (d=4, 6, 8, 9) — literature gap
description: Literature gap from docs/physics/qudit_magic_gate_survey.md §1.5. Watson 2015 Eq. 7 gives T_{3,6}=γ^(n̂³), γ=e^(2πi/9) at d=3; Campbell 2014 gives M_1=ω^(n̂³) at prime d≥5. For d∈{4,6,8,9,…} no canonical qudit-T is published. Three candidate approaches: (a) Watson-style higher-root-of-unity cubic at γ=e^(2πi/(d·a)); (b) CRT tensor factorisation for composite d (d=6=2⊗3) — problematic because SUM mod d ≠ tensor SUM; (c) Galois-field F_{p^k} formalism for prime-power d (Gottesman 1998 §2). Non-blocking: v0.1 ships T_d! for d∈{2,3} and prime d≥5 only. Research bead — deliverable docs/physics/nonprime_qudit_t.md with chosen approach + citations.

title: Harmoniq quantum data augmentation (Kirova-Dörfler-Luef-Kueng 2026) — qudit-based QML primitive
description: Kirova, Dörfler, Luef, Kueng arXiv:2604.18691 (April 2026) introduces Harmoniq — a non-variational quantum data augmentation protocol inspired by quantum harmonic analysis (Werner 1984). Core channel: P_Λ(ρ) = Σ_{(x,z) ∈ Ω} λ(x,z) · W(x,z) · ρ · W(x,z)† where W(x,z) = e^(-iπxz/d) Z_d^z X_d^x is a Weyl-Heisenberg operator on a d-dimensional qudit (d = 2^n), Ω ⊂ Z_d^2 is a localised augmentation window with |Ω| ≪ d^2, and λ is a probability distribution over Ω. Operationally: encode dataset F as mixed density matrix ρ = Σ p_i |ψ_i⟩⟨ψ_i| via stochastic amplitude encoding (random sample i → pure state, repeat), then apply P_Λ via quantum channel. Paper demonstrates on signal denoising with downstream qPCA; augmented covariance matrix has sharper spectrum, improving small-sample regime. Sturm impact — once qudit support (bead goi) lands: implement a function with signature augment_harmoniq(rho::Channel, window::Vector{Tuple{Int,Int}}, weights::Vector{Float64}) returning a Channel, in a new src/qml/ module (or src/library/). Sturm Channel algebra + stochastic mixture (CasesNode-like branches over weight-sampled W unitaries) maps this cleanly. Functions-are-channels (P1) + dimension-agnostic (P7) make this a natural home — fewer lines than a matrix-algebra implementation. Follow-on: chain Harmoniq → qPCA → classification/denoising as end-to-end QML pipeline. Refs: docs/physics/kirova_2026_harmoniq_qml_data_augmentation.pdf + .tar.gz.
acceptance_criteria: augment_harmoniq(rho, window, weights) returns a Channel realising the P_Λ map; verified against reference numpy simulation of the convolution channel on a small d=4 density matrix to 1e-10; end-to-end test on a toy denoising instance (paper Fig 1 style) showing eigenvalue spectrum sharpening.
notes:
BLOCKERS (filed 2026-05-01 audit):
- Sturm.jl-2bf  (P3) — QMod{4} Ry, 6-Givens decomposition. Critical: needed to prep arbitrary input states |psi_i> for the d=4 dataset encoding.
- Sturm.jl-rga4 (P3) — F_d! at d>=3. Once F_4 ships (Cooley-Tukey: F_4 = (F_2 tensor F_2) * CPHASE_4), the rest follows.
- Sturm.jl-w9y1 (P3) — X_d! at d>=3. Trivial once F_d ships (X_d = F_d_dag * Z_d * F_d).
- Sturm.jl-kzh6 (P3) — SUM at d>=4. Only relevant if multi-register Harmoniq is needed; single-qudit Harmoniq does not require it.

Implementation order recommended:
1. Close 2bf (QMod{4} Ry). Unblocks state prep.
2. Close rga4 (F_4 via Cooley-Tukey). Smallest power-of-2 case is the easiest entry point.
3. Close w9y1 (X_4 from F_4). One-liner.
4. Implement augment_harmoniq in src/qml/harmoniq.jl: build W(x,z) = Z_d^z * X_d^x as composition, then convex-sum via DensityMatrixContext Kraus mix or cases().
5. Verify against numpy reference at d=4 to 1e-10 (paper Fig 1 instance).

Trivial-case fallback at d=2: runnable today, but degenerate (Weyl-Heisenberg group at d=2 is the Pauli group; the augmentation reduces to a weighted Pauli / depolarising channel). Useful only as a unit-test smoke for the channel-composition plumbing.

title: QEVT — quantum eigenvalue transformation for arbitrary matrices (Gutiérrez-Laneve-Sanz 2026)
description: Gutiérrez, Laneve, Sanz arXiv:2604.19688 (April 2026) extends QSP/QSVT to non-Hermitian, non-diagonalizable square matrices. Key construct: n-regular block encoding — a block encoding U_A whose k-th power reproduces A^k for every 0 ≤ k ≤ n. The paper proves any block encoding can be converted to n-regular using O(log n) ancillas + O(poly log n) operations; applying GQSP (generalized QSP, which works on the full unit disk vs QSP/QSVT on the unit circle / Hermitian matrices) to an n-regular block-encoding yields a polynomial of the **eigenvalues** (acting on the Jordan normal form) — not singular values. Applications listed: simulation of general inhomogeneous differential equations, non-unitary dynamics via Carleman linearisation, PDEs, open quantum systems. Sturm impact — extend src/qsvt/: (a) GQSP phase computation (circle/disk polynomials, existing phase_factors.jl generalises); (b) nregular_block_encode(U, n) wrapper adding the log(n)-ancilla lift; (c) qevt!(U, poly) primitive that applies a polynomial of eigenvalues; (d) tests on Jordan-block and companion-matrix examples where QSVT cannot act (singular values ≠ eigenvalues). Complements mt9 (QSVT epic) — eigenvalue filter beyond Hermitian. Refs: docs/physics/gutierrez_2026_qevt_arbitrary_matrices.pdf + .tar.gz.
acceptance_criteria: GQSP phase computation + nregular_block_encode + qevt!; end-to-end test: build a Jordan block J of size 3×3 (non-diagonalizable), construct its block encoding, apply QEVT with a polynomial p, verify output block-encodes p(J) within the n-regular ancilla subspace to 1e-8 tolerance.

title: Harden block_encoding PREPARE/SELECT against X!↔Y! convention drift

title: QBool(p) do q … end do-block allocation (Julia open()-style)
description: Add a do-block constructor for short-lived qubits, mirroring Julia's open(f, path) do stream … end. Form: QBool(p::Real) do q::QBool … end runs the body with q in scope and partial-traces q at exit (regardless of normal exit / exception). Same for QInt{W}(value) do reg … end. Implementation: new method QBool(f::Function, p::Real) (and QBool(f::Function, ctx::AbstractContext, p::Real)) that allocates, runs f(q), then auto-discards. Symmetric for QInt. title: QBool/QInt have no finalizer — missing discard! leaks qubit slots
description: src/types/qbool.jl, src/types/qint.jl construct via allocate!(ctx) but have no Julia finalizer. If a user writes `q = QBool(0.5)` inside a function and the function returns without measuring or discarding q, the WireID is unreachable but the Orkan qubit slot stays allocated until the @context block exits. Loop usage hits MAX_QUBITS=30 (loud error per src/context/eager.jl:53) within ~30 iterations — footgun, not silent leak. Fix options: (a) finalizer(q -> if !q.consumed; @async discard!(q.ctx, q.wire); end), (b) RAII-style `@locals` macro auto-discarding on scope exit. Caveat: GC timing is non-deterministic; finalizers calling FFI need @async guarding because Julia GC runs in arbitrary contexts. Discovered during 2026-04-21 resource-lifecycle audit.

title: _ORACLE_TABLE_CACHE has no eviction policy — unbounded memory growth
description: src/bennett/bridge.jl:335 defines _ORACLE_TABLE_CACHE::Dict{Tuple{UInt64,Int,Int},ReversibleCircuit} keyed on (hash(data), W_in, W_out). No LRU, no max size, no cleanup. A long-running Julia session that calls oracle_table with distinct lookup tables (e.g., a hot loop quantising a continuous parameter into different tables, or repeated calls with mutated data arrays) grows the cache by one entry per unique data hash forever. Fix options: (a) LRU with configurable max size (default ~64 entries), (b) WeakRef-based cache that lets GC reclaim entries, (c) explicit clear_oracle_cache!() public API + leave eviction to the user. Discovered during 2026-04-21 resource-lifecycle audit.

title: Pure coset state via comparison-negation — Gidney 1905.08488 Fig 1 full
description: Current _coset_init! (Sturm.jl-8fy rewrite, commit 234b8ef) uses Cpad EXTERNAL pad-ancilla wires that remain entangled with reg after init, yielding the mixed-state (1/√2^Cpad) Σ_j |j⟩_pad ⊗ |k+jN⟩_reg. Pragmatic for 6xi acceptance but not the Gidney Fig 1 circuit. The paper's PURE-STATE construction uses a (-1)^{x≥2^p·N} comparison-negation phase kickback per stage to DISENTANGLE the pad ancillae back to |0⟩, yielding the single-register coset state (1/√2^Cpad) Σ_j |k+jN⟩ with NO external ancillae remaining. Benefits: (a) reduces steady-state qubit count by Cpad — 3 qubits for Cpad=3, significant at bigger N; (b) matches the paper for downstream code/publication; (c) eliminates the pad-ancilla partial-trace step in decode!; (d) unblocks true Gidney-style coset arithmetic across the rest of the stack (e.g. runway/windowed reuse the pure state).
design: Implement reversible comparator circuit _comparison_negate!(reg::QInt{W}, threshold::Integer) that applies (-1)^{reg ≥ threshold} phase kickback on reg. Likely approach: compute (reg - threshold) into a temporary W+1-bit sign register (using sub_qft_quantum!), check sign bit, apply Z on that sign bit, uncompute the subtraction. New primitive in src/library/arithmetic.jl. Then rewrite _coset_init! to follow Gidney Fig 1 literally: for p=0..Cpad-1 sequentially: allocate pad_p fresh in |0⟩, H!(pad_p), when(pad_p) { add_qft!(reg, 2^p·N) }, _comparison_negate!(reg, 2^p·N), H!(pad_p), verify pad_p ends in |0⟩ and deallocate. title: compact_state! :unsafe_copyto! shortcut for contiguous-live case
description: compact_state! (src/context/eager.jl) currently always runs the bit-scatter loop, even when live slots are already 0..k-1 contiguous and the only thing wrong is n_qubits being too high. Cost: cheap to detect, ~O(2^new_n / 2^old_n) cheaper to copy. Estimated win: a few percent on small contexts; no win on Bennett-burst patterns where freed slots are scattered.
